questions.stem: Which grammar gives multiple parse trees for the same string?
questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.

answer.explanation: COMP10 defines ambiguity by the existence of one terminal string with two different parse trees. This is exactly the property asked for. An unambiguous grammar excludes it. Being regular describes a grammar class rather than guaranteeing multiple trees, so it does not make all the listed descriptions correct.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Unambiguous means each generated string has a unique parse tree, directly contradicting the property.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Regularity restricts grammar form; it does not require multiple parse trees for a string.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Ambiguity is precisely the existence of multiple parse trees for the same terminal string.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Unambiguous grammars do not have the stated property, so all cannot be correct.

evidence.quote: A grammar is ambiguous if at least one terminal string has two different parse trees, equivalently two leftmost derivations. Merely changing derivation order on the same tree does not establish ambiguity. E→E+E|E*E|id allows different trees for id+id*id.

Use E→E+T|T, T→T*F|F, F→(E)|id to give * higher precedence and both operators left associativity. For subtraction, a−b−c then groups (a−b)−c. The dangling-else grammar permits else to attach to either nested if; a nearest-unmatched-if rule or grammar rewrite resolves it. Taking a leftmost derivation by itself does not resolve ambiguous interpretation.

questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 47

answer.explanation: Scanning reads characters and represents matched lexemes as tokens (PDF pp. 5, 8). Syntax analysis then groups those tokens and produces a parse tree. Building that tree is therefore the non-lexical task.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Grouping characters into matched lexemes belongs to scanning (pp. 5, 8).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A sequence of tokens is the scanner’s stated output (p. 8).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Reading the stream of source characters is explicitly lexical analysis.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Constructing the syntactic tree belongs to syntax analysis.

evidence.quote: Keywords, identifiers, literals, operators and punctuation are token classes. Whitespace and comments are usually skipped while line/column positions are retained. In indentation-sensitive or newline-sensitive languages, layout can carry tokens. Parse-tree construction is a parser task; scanning can intern identifier spellings, but declaration scope and types need later analysis.
A parse tree shows grammar productions: root S, internal nonterminals, and terminal leaves, with ε sometimes shown for empty productions. Its left-to-right yield is the input.

questions.stem: Which statement is false about a compiler parser that constructs a parse tree and supports syntax-error diagnosis and recovery?

options.label: B
options.text: Parser attempts to correct or recover few errors

options.label: C
options.text: Parser cannot perform  context free syntax analysis

questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 54

answer.text: Parser cannot perform  context free syntax analysis
answer.explanation: A parser analyzes the token stream against the context-free syntax and builds its structural representation. In a compiler with syntax diagnostics and recovery, it can report an unexpected token and try to resume at a useful boundary. Therefore the claim that it cannot perform context-free syntax analysis reverses its defining role. Building a parse tree, reporting syntax errors and attempting the specified recovery behavior are compatible responsibilities.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Building a parse tree represents the grammar structure recognized by syntax analysis.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Error recovery may skip to a synchronization token or make a limited local repair.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Context-free syntax analysis is the parser’s defining task, so denying it is false.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Syntax diagnostics identify unexpected or missing tokens with useful source locations.

evidence.quote: A context-free grammar G=(N,T,P,S) has nonterminals N, terminals T, productions P and start S. A production A→α rewrites one nonterminal.
A parse tree shows grammar productions: root S, internal nonterminals, and terminal leaves, with ε sometimes shown for empty productions. Its left-to-right yield is the input.

Panic-mode recovery skips input until a synchronizing token such as ; or } permits parsing to resume. Phrase-level recovery makes a local insertion/deletion. Report the location and cause while avoiding cascades of misleading diagnostics. Lexical, syntax and semantic phases each detect their own errors; error handling is a shared service.

questions.stem: For an infix source expression targeting a postfix stack evaluator, which notation conversion prepares it for evaluation?

options.label: A
options.text: Convert infix notation to postfix notation

options.label: B
options.text: Convert postfix notation to prefix notation

options.label: C
options.text: Evaluate infix notation to prefix notation

questions.hint: Track where each computed value comes from and when each production action runs. Distinguish the representation from its attached information.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 58

answer.text: Convert infix notation to postfix notation
answer.explanation: A postfix evaluator reads operands before the operator that combines them. Converting an infix expression to postfix therefore supplies the required input order for the specified stack target. For example, the tree for a−4+c yields a 4 − c + in postorder. This is a choice of representation for this evaluator, rather than a mandatory strategy for every compiler.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Infix-to-postfix supplies the required target order.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Neither source nor target matches this direction.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Prefix is not the specified target.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This reverses the specified translation direction.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed translation scheme embeds executable actions in productions; the actions run while translating a source program, not while generating the compiler. Attributes may compute types, values, AST pointers or generated code. The scheme defines an input-to-output translation, not merely an input language.

Create an identifier leaf with mkleaf(id,entry), a number with mkleaf(num,value), and an operator node with mknode(op,left,right). For a−4+c, construct +(−(a,4),c). Postorder traversal prints postfix: a 4 − c +. A stack evaluator pushes operands and pops right then left operands for an operator. Infix-to-postfix is useful for stack machines but not mandatory for all compilers.

questions.stem: Which named transformation directly replaces an expression whose operands are compile-time constants with its computed value?
questions.hint: Trace whether computation is evaluated, moved, shared or removed. Preserve observable effects and use the stated arithmetic and target assumptions.
sources: University of Gondar model exam · Question 66

answer.explanation: Constant folding evaluates an expression from operands known at compilation and substitutes its value, such as replacing 3*4 with 12. This removes that expression’s run-time arithmetic. A peephole pass describes a small inspection region and may perform several transformations; it is not the particular evaluation rule. Loop-invariant computation can remain unknown until execution, and hoisting moves safe invariant work rather than necessarily computing a compile-time value.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Peephole identifies a short-window optimization method, not specifically constant-expression evaluation.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Constant folding computes a known constant expression during compilation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: An invariant may depend on a run-time input even though it stays unchanged across a loop.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Hoisting moves a computation to a preheader; it need not evaluate it at compilation.

evidence.quote: Constant folding evaluates constant expressions during compilation: 3*4→12.
A loop-invariant expression has unchanged inputs during a loop. Hoist it to a preheader only when evaluation is safe on the paths where it will newly run.
Peephole optimization examines short instruction windows.

questions.stem: Which listed deterministic parser families can evaluate synthesized attributes for suitable grammars and semantic actions? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Track where each computed value comes from and when each production action runs. Distinguish the representation from its attached information.
sources: University of Gondar model exam · Question 68

answer.explanation: Synthesized attributes flow from child nodes to their parent. LR parsers naturally compute these during reduction, after the right-hand-side children have been recognized. Suitable LL implementations can also compute them after their recursive child calls return. Ambiguity is a property of grammar interpretation, not a deterministic parser family or attribute-evaluation method. Thus both LR and LL are valid families for this task.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Ambiguity is not a deterministic parser family or evaluation mechanism.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: LR reduction actions can compute parent values from children.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Suitable LL actions can compute values after child processing.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Both LR and LL provide supported implementations.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions. An annotated parse tree displays computed attribute values; it is not itself an inherited or synthesized attribute. Synthesized attributes flow from children to a parent; inherited attributes carry context from parent or siblings.

For E→E1+T, E.val=E1.val+T.val synthesizes an expression value. A declaration’s type environment passed into its body is inherited. S-attributed definitions use only synthesized attributes and fit LR reduction-time evaluation naturally; suitable LL parsers can also compute them. L-attributed definitions restrict dependencies so a left-to-right traversal can evaluate inherited context. Attribute dependency cycles can prevent evaluation.

questions.stem: Identifiers consist of one Letter followed by zero or more Letters or Digits. Which expressions denote exactly that language? Select all that apply. Here + means one-or-more, | alternation, and _ a literal underscore.
questions.hint: Follow the representation at each construction step and apply the pattern or state-set rules consistently, including empty cases.
sources: University of Gondar model exam · Question 69

answer.explanation: C directly expresses a leading letter followed by any sequence of letters and digits. A is equivalent: its outer star may take zero blocks, and repeated letter or digit blocks can generate every such suffix. B excludes a one-letter identifier because its suffix uses plus. D permits literal underscores and restricted digit blocks, so it does not denote the specified identifier language.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Its repeated blocks generate every allowed suffix, including the empty suffix.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The trailing plus excludes a one-letter identifier.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This directly states the required pattern.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Its literal underscores violate the specified alphabet and its restricted suffix misses identifiers.

evidence.quote: Regular expressions use concatenation, alternation r|s, Kleene star r* for zero or more, and r+ for one or more. In a simplified alphabet, identifier = Letter(Letter|Digit)*; it permits a single letter and forbids a leading digit.

Letter(Letter+|Digit*)* denotes the same language as Letter(Letter|Digit)* under ordinary regular-expression semantics: repeated blocks can contain any trailing letter/digit sequence. These two regular expressions are equivalent. Regular patterns handle ordinary tokens; arbitrary balanced nesting generally needs grammar/stack structure.

questions.stem: For a register-based target compiler, which choice most completely lists general code-generator tasks?
questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.

answer.explanation: COMP34 separates selecting target operations, deciding storage in registers, assigning physical registers, and scheduling instructions. The three concrete choices name these standard code-generation tasks. Since the question offers an aggregate covering them, that aggregate is the complete answer; each individual choice supplies only part of the requested task list.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Instruction selection chooses which target instructions implement the intermediate operations.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Register allocation and physical assignment decide where values reside and which registers hold them.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Instruction ordering schedules computations while preserving data and control dependencies.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: All three listed activities belong to the code-generator task set described in COMP34.

evidence.quote: Code generation lowers checked IR to a target form. Instruction selection chooses target operations; register allocation chooses where values reside; scheduling orders instructions while respecting dependencies; storage layout assigns offsets and follows ABI requirements. Register assignment names actual physical registers after allocation decisions.

For t=a+b, a simple target could emit LOAD R1,a; LOAD R2,b; ADD R3,R1,R2; STORE t,R3. Other targets may combine loads with arithmetic or keep t in a register. Machine idioms, register availability and instruction order affect execution time.

answer.explanation: A lexeme is the sequence of characters matched by a pattern to form a token (PDF p. 8). A token instead denotes a class of similar lexemes, and a pattern specifies the rule. “Specific character strings” therefore identifies lexemes.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Token names the class in the module’s token/lexeme distinction (p. 8).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Lexemes are the actual matched sequences (p. 8).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Lexical units is not the defined name for specific strings in this passage (p. 8).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A pattern is the matching rule, not its particular match (p. 8).

evidence.quote: A token is a category with optional attribute, such as (ID, symbol-entry) or (INT_LITERAL,42). A lexeme is the actual character sequence, such as total or 42. A pattern specifies which lexemes belong to a token class. The scanner emits an ordered token stream, not an unordered mathematical set.

Keywords, identifiers, literals, operators and punctuation are token classes. Whitespace and comments are usually skipped while line/column positions are retained. In indentation-sensitive or newline-sensitive languages, layout can carry tokens. Parse-tree construction is a parser task; scanning can intern identifier spellings, but declaration scope and types need later analysis.

questions.stem: Which one of the following are the program properties that can be checked at run time?
questions.hint: Ask whether the required information is a declaration’s identity and attributes, program structure or the ordered source tokens.

answer.explanation: Semantic checks are static when done during compilation and dynamic when done during run-time (PDF p. 14). Interpreting “Dynamic semantics” as the option’s name for run-time semantic checking, B fits; static checking and other static checks occur during compilation.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Static checking is done at compilation, not run-time (p. 14).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: B corresponds to the module’s run-time dynamic semantic checks (p. 14).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Other static checks retain the compile-time timing (p. 14).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: None does not fit because the dynamic check category is present (p. 14).

evidence.quote: Static checks occur before execution: type compatibility, duplicate declarations within a restricted scope, valid names, argument counts, return compatibility and control-flow placement. A break is valid only in constructs allowed by the language; in C/C++ it can exit a loop or switch. A compiler may annotate an AST or create typed IR; there is no mandatory uniquely named output tree.

Dynamic checks depend on runtime values, such as some bounds and null checks. Static analysis can prove some accesses safe or faulty; “all memory errors cannot be statically checked” is too strong. Unreachable code is not universally a semantic error: some languages reject it in specified cases, others merely warn or optimize it away.

options.label: A
options.text: Stripping out blanks, tabs, new lines

questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.

answer.explanation: COMP04 says scanners usually skip whitespace and comments while retaining source positions. COMP39 adds that lexical analysis detects its own errors and that error handling is shared. These establish all three listed secondary scanner duties under the ordinary language convention. Layout-sensitive languages are an explicit exception in COMP04, not evidence that scanners never perform these tasks.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Comments are normally discarded instead of being delivered as ordinary parser tokens.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Lexical errors require reporting, with positions retained to locate the offending source text.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Together the choices cover normal whitespace removal, comment removal and lexical error reporting.

questions.hint: Track where each computed value comes from and when each production action runs. Distinguish the representation from its attached information.

answer.explanation: COMP24 directly calls a parse tree displaying computed attribute values an annotated parse tree. Inherited and synthesized classify how attribute information flows; neither is the name of the entire displayed tree. Combining those attribute categories still does not name the representation described in the question.

choices.label: A

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions. An annotated parse tree displays computed attribute values; it is not itself an inherited or synthesized attribute. Synthesized attributes flow from children to a parent; inherited attributes carry context from parent or siblings.

For E→E1+T, E.val=E1.val+T.val synthesizes an expression value. A declaration’s type environment passed into its body is inherited. questions.stem:
Which one of the following can be applied directly after intermediate code generation to
improve the intermediate representation?
questions.hint: Trace whether computation is evaluated, moved, shared or removed. Preserve observable effects and use the stated arithmetic and target assumptions.

answer.explanation: Optimization changes intermediate code to remove inefficiencies (PDF p. 7). The module lists peephole transformations and constant propagation (p. 18), and elimination of never-executed or unreachable statements (p. 18). Each can improve an intermediate representation before target code is emitted; no exclusive ordering among those transformations is specified.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Peephole transformation improves instruction sequences (p. 18).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Constant propagation is a listed optimization technique (p. 18).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Removing unreachable intermediate statements is dead code elimination (p. 18).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: All three fit the optimization of intermediate code described on p. 7.

evidence.quote: Constant folding evaluates constant expressions during compilation: 3*4→12. Constant propagation substitutes known values: x=3; y=x+2 becomes y=3+2 before folding. Copy propagation substitutes a copied name while its source remains unchanged. Dead-code elimination removes unreachable code or computations whose values are unused and whose evaluation has no necessary side effects.

Common-subexpression elimination reuses an earlier value only if operand values and relevant memory remain unchanged. A DAG can represent sharing. Algebraic simplification removes identities when valid: integer x+0→x. Strength reduction replaces an operation with an equivalent cheaper form, such as unsigned x*8→x<<3 for a valid width and shift count. Target costs determine whether it is actually cheaper.

Peephole optimization examines short instruction windows. It can remove redundant loads/stores, replace machine idioms and shorten jump chains: jump L1 where L1 immediately jumps L2 can become jump L2. Local optimization is a wider category; peephole optimization is a concrete method within the relevant scope.

questions.stem: Which compiler structure associates declared identifier names or identities with attributes such as type, scope and storage location, irrespective of its container implementation?
questions.hint: Ask whether the required information is a declaration’s identity and attributes, program structure or the ordered source tokens.

answer.explanation: A symbol table maps identifier names or declaration identities to attributes such as type, scope and storage location. A hash table is one possible implementation of that mapping, not its semantic role. Literal tables concern literal values, and punctuation need not have symbol records at all. Restricting the question to identifier metadata avoids claiming that every token kind uses the same table.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A literal table concerns literal values.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The symbol table provides this mapping.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Hashing is an implementation technique rather than the semantic role.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The structures have different roles.

evidence.quote: A symbol table maps names or symbol identities to attributes: type, scope, width, storage offset, parameter signature, constant information or linkage. A hash table gives expected O(1) insertion/lookup with suitable hashing; a stack of scope tables supports lexical nesting. Search the nearest scope first, insert declarations in the current scope, and remove visibility when leaving it.

Scanning may intern a spelling first; semantic analysis determines the declaration and type. Implementations differ, so first interaction is conventional rather than universal. Not every punctuation token needs a symbol-table entry; literals may use a separate literal table. A hash table is an implementation, not the information’s semantic role.
Grouping characters into token classes is lexical analysis; grouping tokens into expressions and statements is syntax analysis.
Trees store hierarchical constructs, while a symbol table stores declaration metadata.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT the primary role of code generator in compiler design? *
questions.hint: Identify what the representation stores, what it omits and which later transformations it must support; separate a representation property from an algorithmic task.

answer.explanation: Code generation lowers checked intermediate code into target operations. It selects instructions, allocates registers and orders instructions subject to dependencies. Declarations instead establish source names, types and storage information during analysis; generating code may use that information without declaring the variables again. Thus the declaration activity is outside the primary code-generator task set, while the other three choices describe target implementation decisions.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Instruction selection chooses target operations implementing the IR.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Processing source declarations belongs to analysis and symbol-table/type handling.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Instruction ordering schedules target computations while preserving dependencies.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Register allocation decides where intermediate values reside.

evidence.quote: IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. It should be easy to generate, analyze, transform and lower.

Ordinary TAC arithmetic has at most one operation, two sources and one destination: t1=c*d; t2=b+t1; a=t2. Quadruples store (op,arg1,arg2,result); triples omit an explicit result field and refer to instruction positions. Indirect triples reference a separate ordering list, easing rearrangement. Trees describe expressions; DAGs share common subexpressions, while quadruples/triples are instruction-record structures.

Code generation lowers checked IR to a target form. Instruction selection chooses target operations; register allocation chooses where values reside; scheduling orders instructions while respecting dependencies; storage layout assigns offsets and follows ABI requirements. Register assignment names actual physical registers after allocation decisions.

For t=a+b, a simple target could emit LOAD R1,a; LOAD R2,b; ADD R3,R1,R2; STORE t,R3. Other targets may combine loads with arithmetic or keep t in a register. Machine idioms, register availability and instruction order affect execution time.

questions.stem: A compiler computes expression-type attributes and checks compatibility as grammar productions are processed. Which offered description most specifically identifies this mechanism?
questions.hint: Check operand compatibility and permitted conversions under the stated language rules; distinguish grammatical structure from semantic meaning.

answer.explanation: The compiler in the scenario evaluates type attributes and applies compatibility checks as grammar productions are processed. This is syntax-directed translation: semantic rules or actions are attached to grammatical structure. Pure lexical analysis only recognizes tokens, and pure syntax recognition alone does not establish operand-type compatibility. Optimization transforms an already analyzed representation. Parsing can invoke these semantic actions, so the mechanism is more precise than naming syntax analysis alone.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Token recognition alone does not compute full expression-type compatibility.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Pure syntax recognition checks grammar; the scenario additionally attaches semantic computations.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Syntax-directed semantic actions compute and check attributes associated with productions.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Optimization transforms analyzed code rather than naming the stated checking mechanism.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions.

A syntax-directed translation scheme embeds executable actions in productions; the actions run while translating a source program, not while generating the compiler. Attributes may compute types, values, AST pointers or generated code.

A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Function calls check parameter count and compatibility, and returns match result types.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions. questions.stem: Which one of the following is a top-down parser without backtracking?
questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.

answer.explanation: COMP11 defines predictive parsing by choosing productions with lookahead without backtracking. This supplies both requirements in the stem: top-down direction and absence of backtracking. LR and operator-precedence parsing belong to bottom-up approaches; brute-force top-down trial does not provide the no-backtracking guarantee.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: LR parsing reduces input bottom-up rather than expanding the start symbol top-down.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Brute-force production trials can require backtracking and do not meet the defining predictive constraint.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Operator-precedence parsing is a bottom-up technique rather than predictive top-down expansion.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Predictive parsing uses lookahead to choose productions without backtracking, exactly as COMP11 states.

evidence.quote: Top-down parsing starts with S and expands productions toward the input, usually constructing a leftmost derivation. Recursive descent typically has one procedure per nonterminal. A general recursive-descent implementation can backtrack; a predictive parser chooses a production using lookahead without backtracking. LL(1) scans Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation and uses one lookahead token.
Bottom-up parsing starts from input and reduces toward S, constructing a rightmost derivation in reverse.

Operator-precedence parsing is a restricted bottom-up expression-parsing method using a stack and precedence relations. With a suitable expression grammar, the stack retains unfinished surrounding expressions while nested parentheses are processed.

options.label: A
options.text: Code generation can be considered as the start phase of compilation

options.label: B
options.text: The target program is the output of the code generator

options.label: C

answer.text: Code generation can be considered as the start phase of compilation
answer.explanation: Lexical analysis begins the standard pipeline by recognizing tokens. Code generation occurs after analysis and IR construction, lowering checked IR to a target form. Its output is target code, which may be assembly or an object form, and it can translate three-address statements. Therefore calling code generation the start phase is the wrong description. The input option is read as checked IR suitable for lowering, without claiming a compiler can prove the absence of every program defect.

choices.explanation: Code generation follows the frontend and IR; it is not the initial scanning phase.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The generator produces code in a target representation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Checked intermediate code supplies the operations and metadata to lower.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Three-address statements can be lowered into target instructions.

questions.stem: Which is the least sufficient Chomsky grammar family for ordinary token patterns specified by classical regular expressions, rather than a purpose-based grammar name?
questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 93

answer.explanation: Ordinary regular-expression token patterns describe regular languages, whose least sufficient Chomsky family is regular grammar. A lexical grammar names a specification by purpose, whereas this question asks for its formal family. Context-free grammars are more expressive than required and typically model nested syntax. Syntactic grammar is another purpose label rather than the specific formal family matching the regular token patterns.

choices.explanation: Lexical grammar is a purpose label, not the requested family.

choices.explanation: CFGs are stronger than these regular patterns require.

choices.explanation: Syntactic grammar is a purpose label.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Regular grammars generate exactly regular token languages.

evidence.quote: Classical regular expressions, consistently right-linear regular grammars and finite automata describe the same regular-language family. Thus an ordinary token pattern specified by a regular expression also has a regular grammar and an equivalent finite-state recognizer.

This equivalence concerns expressive power, not spelling of the specification or implementation size. Context-free grammars can also describe regular languages, but their larger family is needed for syntax with unbounded nested structure rather than ordinary regular token patterns.
Regular patterns are chiefly lexical specifications; CFGs chiefly describe nested syntax.

questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.

answer.explanation: COMP11 introduces recursive descent as a top-down implementation, normally with one procedure per nonterminal. It expands the start symbol toward the input. LR and LALR instead use bottom-up reductions, and operator-precedence parsing is also bottom-up. Therefore only recursive descent names the top-down family among these options.

choices.label: A

choices.explanation: Operator-precedence parsing reduces expressions bottom-up rather than expanding productions top-down.

evidence.quote: Top-down parsing starts with S and expands productions toward the input, usually constructing a leftmost derivation. Recursive descent typically has one procedure per nonterminal. A general recursive-descent implementation can backtrack; a predictive parser chooses a production using lookahead without backtracking. LL(1) scans Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation and uses one lookahead token.
Bottom-up parsing starts from input and reduces toward S, constructing a rightmost derivation in reverse.

Operator-precedence parsing is a restricted bottom-up expression-parsing method using a stack and precedence relations. With a suitable expression grammar, the stack retains unfinished surrounding expressions while nested parentheses are processed.

evidence.quote: A basic block is a maximal straight-line instruction sequence entered at its beginning and exited at its end. Leaders are the first instruction, every jump target, and each instruction after a branch. Start a block at each leader and continue until the next leader.

A control-flow graph has blocks as vertices and possible next-block transfers as edges, including fall-through. A node D dominates N when every entry-to-N path passes through D. For an edge N→H where H dominates N, H is a loop header of a natural loop. This structure supports loop analysis. An expression DAG records value dependencies, not arbitrary control flow.

answer.explanation: COMP26 explains that IR separates source analysis from target implementation, making optimizers and backends reusable. evidence.quote: IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. It should be easy to generate, analyze, transform and lower.

evidence.quote: A loop-invariant expression has unchanged inputs during a loop. Hoist it to a preheader only when evaluation is safe on the paths where it will newly run. answer.explanation: COMP12 writes immediate left recursion as A→Aα: the production’s left-hand nonterminal occurs first on its right-hand side. This is precisely the pattern in the question. Leftmost derivation chooses which nonterminal to expand; left factoring extracts a shared prefix. Neither is the repeated-leftmost-self-reference property.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A production beginning with its own left-hand nonterminal is immediate left recursion.

evidence.quote:
Immediate left recursion has A→Aα. For A→Aα|β, where β does not start with A, introduce a new nonterminal A′ and use:
A→βA′
A′→αA′|ε
This preserves the generated language; tree shape changes, so semantic actions must preserve intended associativity. Indirect left recursion follows a cycle through other nonterminals and also needs removal for ordinary predictive descent.

Left factoring rewrites A→αβ|αγ using:
A→αA′
A′→β|γ
It postpones a choice until after the common prefix. It does not by itself remove ambiguity or guarantee LL(1). LR parsers can handle suitable left-recursive grammars; ordinary unmodified recursive descent can recurse forever before consuming input.

evidence.quote: Bottom-up parsing starts from input and reduces toward S, constructing a rightmost derivation in reverse. A handle is a production RHS occurrence whose reduction is the next step of that reverse derivation. Not every substring matching a RHS is a handle in the current context.

evidence.quote: Panic-mode recovery skips input until a synchronizing token such as ; or } permits parsing to resume. Phrase-level recovery makes a local insertion/deletion. answer.explanation: An operator grammar explicitly forbids adjacent nonterminals on a right-hand side. A consistently right-linear regular grammar has at most one nonterminal in such a rule, so it also guarantees the restriction. Arbitrary unrestricted grammars have no comparable adjacency guarantee. evidence.quote: A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Function calls check parameter count and compatibility, and returns match result types.

Type inference derives types from constraints: if x is integer and + expects numeric operands, infer the expression type from numeric promotion rules. It is a static technique even without explicit annotations. Operator overloading supplies multiple operation meanings, not a substitute for type checking. int x="hello" is a type mismatch in ordinary C++/Java; division by zero and bounds violations are not automatically operand-type mismatches.

answer.text: Parsing with explicit operator precedence and left-associativity rules
answer.explanation: The grammar permits multiple groupings of expressions such as id+id*id. An explicit precedence and associativity policy selects multiplication before addition and left association within each level. A parser may enforce this through declarations or a grammar rewrite. Lexical analysis and generic semantic checking do not themselves establish that policy, and taking a leftmost derivation does not remove the competing parse trees.

evidence.quote: A grammar is ambiguous if at least one terminal string has two different parse trees, equivalently two leftmost derivations. Merely changing derivation order on the same tree does not establish ambiguity. E→E+E|E*E|id allows different trees for id+id*id.

Use E→E+T|T, T→T*F|F, F→(E)|id to give * higher precedence and both operators left associativity. For subtraction, a−b−c then groups (a−b)−c. The dangling-else grammar permits else to attach to either nested if; a nearest-unmatched-if rule or grammar rewrite resolves it. Taking a leftmost derivation by itself does not resolve ambiguous interpretation.

answer.text: To perform type checking and enforce semantic rules

evidence.quote: A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Function calls check parameter count and compatibility, and returns match result types.

Type inference derives types from constraints: if x is integer and + expects numeric operands, infer the expression type from numeric promotion rules. It is a static technique even without explicit annotations. Operator overloading supplies multiple operation meanings, not a substitute for type checking. int x="hello" is a type mismatch in ordinary C++/Java; division by zero and bounds violations are not automatically operand-type mismatches.

evidence.quote: A symbol table maps names or symbol identities to attributes: type, scope, width, storage offset, parameter signature, constant information or linkage. questions.stem: What is the purpose of intermediate code in compiler design?

options.label: C
options.text: To represent the program's semantics in a platform-independent form

options.label: D
options.text: To visualize the program's control flow

questions.hint: Identify what the representation stores, what it omits and which later transformations it must support; separate a representation property from an algorithmic task.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 798

answer.text: Represent program meaning in a reusable, substantially platform-independent intermediate form.
answer.explanation: COMP26 identifies separation of source analysis and target implementation as IR’s architectural purpose, allowing reuse across targets. C expresses that purpose best. Optimization and assembly generation are operations enabled by the representation, while a control-flow graph is one possible representation aspect. Platform independence is a design benefit here, not a claim that every IR has no target details.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Optimization is enabled by IR, but it is not the general representational purpose distinguishing this choice.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Assembly is one possible later output; an IR need not be tied to assembly generation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A reusable representation of program semantics separates front-end meaning from target-specific implementation.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Control-flow visualization is one possible use and does not exhaust the purpose of IR.

evidence.quote: IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. It should be easy to generate, analyze, transform and lower.

Ordinary TAC arithmetic has at most one operation, two sources and one destination: t1=c*d; t2=b+t1; a=t2. Quadruples store (op,arg1,arg2,result); triples omit an explicit result field and refer to instruction positions. Indirect triples reference a separate ordering list, easing rearrangement. Trees describe expressions; DAGs share common subexpressions, while quadruples/triples are instruction-record structures.

questions.stem: Which of the following is used to generate a lexical analyzer for a programming language?
questions.hint: Follow the representation at each construction step and apply the pattern or state-set rules consistently, including empty cases.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 799

answer.explanation: COMP06 describes converting regular expressions to an NFA and then a DFA. This is the automaton construction used for ordinary generated token recognizers. CFGs and pushdown machinery address nested syntax rather than the regular token-pattern mechanism; a Turing machine is not the specific scanner model in the supplied construction.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: NFA/DFA finite automata implement recognition of regular token patterns in the stated generator pipeline.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: CFGs describe nested syntactic structure rather than the regular scanner-automaton construction.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Pushdown machinery adds a stack for context-free structure and is not the ordinary token-recognizer construction.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A Turing machine is more general but is not the specific model used in this scanner-generation pipeline.

evidence.quote: A common generator pipeline is regular expressions → NFA using Thompson construction → DFA using subset construction; minimization is optional. For concatenation rs, connect r’s final state to s’s start by ε. Alternation introduces branching ε paths; star adds a way to skip and repeat the fragment.

The ε-closure of states includes those reachable by zero or more ε edges. A DFA state is a set of NFA states; its a-transition is ε-closure(move(set,a)). Start with the NFA start closure, repeatedly add unseen subsets, and mark subsets containing an NFA final state as accepting. Token identity and rule priority annotate accepting states; the empty subset acts as a dead state.

questions.stem: Which listed notation directly specifies ordinary token patterns using alternation, concatenation and repetition, rather than a general production notation or a tree of one program?
questions.hint: Follow the representation at each construction step and apply the pattern or state-set rules consistently, including empty cases.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 801

answer.explanation: Classical regular expressions combine alternation, concatenation and repetition to specify ordinary token patterns. CFGs and BNF are production-based grammar descriptions and can also describe regular languages, so mere expressive capability would not distinguish them. An AST represents the analyzed structure of a particular program. The revised comparison asks for the direct pattern notation characterized by its operators, making regular expressions the specific answer.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Regular expressions directly use the stated pattern-combination operators.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A CFG is a general production grammar, not the direct expression notation described.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: BNF is a notation for context-free productions.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An AST represents one analyzed program structure rather than the permitted token patterns.

evidence.quote:
Regular expressions use concatenation, alternation r|s, Kleene star r* for zero or more, and r+ for one or more. In a simplified alphabet, identifier = Letter(Letter|Digit)*; it permits a single letter and forbids a leading digit. A C-like ASCII rule commonly also allows underscore:
[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
State the convention instead of claiming this covers every language’s identifiers.

Backus–Naur form, or BNF, is a notation for context-free grammar production rules. It describes how syntactic constructs are formed; it is different from an abstract syntax tree representing one particular program.
An AST omits grammar scaffolding and punctuation; expression operands are leaves and operators internal nodes. The parser can build either representation, depending on implementation.

questions.stem: Which listed parsing approaches can handle arbitrarily nested parenthesized expressions for suitable grammars and stack-based implementations? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 802

answer.text: LL Parsing; LR Parsing; Recursive Descent Parsing; Operator Precedence Parsing
answer.explanation: Nested parentheses require remembering unfinished surrounding expressions. LL and LR parsers use a parsing stack, recursive descent uses the call stack, and suitable operator-precedence expression parsing also uses stack structure and precedence relations. Each can therefore handle the stipulated nested expressions for an appropriate grammar. The existence of nesting alone does not distinguish one of these parser families from the others.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: LL can parse a suitable nested-expression grammar using its stack.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: LR can recognize the nesting with bottom-up stack actions.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Recursive descent processes nested expressions through recursive calls.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A suitable operator-precedence parser supports parenthesized subexpressions.

evidence.quote: LL, LR and recursive-descent parsers can all handle nested parentheses for suitable grammars. An explicit or implicit stack, not the LR label alone, supports unbounded nesting.

Operator-precedence parsing is a restricted bottom-up expression-parsing method using a stack and precedence relations. With a suitable expression grammar, the stack retains unfinished surrounding expressions while nested parentheses are processed.

questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 803

answer.explanation: LR parsing constructs the parse tree bottom-up, reducing handles that correspond to a rightmost derivation in reverse. LL methods construct from the start symbol toward the input and are top-down. Recursive descent normally implements one procedure per nonterminal, also expanding top-down. The generic top-down option states the opposite construction direction. These are implementation and derivation distinctions, not a ranking of their execution speed.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: LL parsing expands a leftmost derivation from the start symbol.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: LR parsing reduces input handles and builds bottom-up.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Recursive-descent procedures expand grammar nonterminals top-down.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Top-down construction starts from the root, the opposite direction.

evidence.quote: Top-down parsing starts with S and expands productions toward the input, usually constructing a leftmost derivation. Recursive descent typically has one procedure per nonterminal. A general recursive-descent implementation can backtrack; a predictive parser chooses a production using lookahead without backtracking. LL(1) scans Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation and uses one lookahead token.
Bottom-up parsing starts from input and reduces toward S, constructing a rightmost derivation in reverse.

answer.explanation: Operator-precedence parsing applies precedence relations to a suitable operator grammar to choose expression parsing actions. The question specifies that concrete method rather than asking for a universal cure for shift/reduce conflicts. Precedence parsing is a broader label, while LR and LL name larger parser families without supplying these particular relations. Therefore B is the most specific match to the described technique.

evidence.quote:
Immediate left recursion has A→Aα. For A→Aα|β, where β does not start with A, introduce a new nonterminal A′ and use:
A→βA′
A′→αA′|ε
This preserves the generated language; tree shape changes, so semantic actions must preserve intended associativity. Indirect left recursion follows a cycle through other nonterminals and also needs removal for ordinary predictive descent.

A→αA′
A′→β|γ
It postpones a choice until after the common prefix. It does not by itself remove ambiguity or guarantee LL(1). LR parsers can handle suitable left-recursive grammars; ordinary unmodified recursive descent can recurse forever before consuming input.

answer.explanation: A general ambiguous grammar has multiple parse trees for at least one input. Recursive descent and top-down labels alone do not provide a generalized multi-parse method, so the GLR alternative uniquely answers the question.

evidence.quote: LL, LR and recursive-descent parsers can all handle nested parentheses for suitable grammars. An explicit or implicit stack, not the LR label alone, supports unbounded nesting. evidence.quote: A compiler translates a source program into an equivalent target representation while preserving defined observable behavior. The target may be machine code, assembly, bytecode or another source language. A transpiler is a source-to-source compiler, not a fundamentally separate noncompiler technology. A compiler preserves language semantics, not the programmer’s unstated intention.

An interpreter executes a program representation; it need not work one source line at a time. Systems can compile to bytecode and then interpret or JIT-compile it. AOT compilation happens before execution; JIT compilation happens during execution and may use runtime profiles. Neither is universally faster; startup cost, optimization and workload matter.

evidence.quote: A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Type inference derives types from constraints: if x is integer and + expects numeric operands, infer the expression type from numeric promotion rules. It is a static technique even without explicit annotations. answer.explanation: COMP19 explicitly says a hash table offers expected constant-time insertion and lookup with suitable hashing. That makes it the conventional structure for the name-to-attribute mapping. A stack can organize nested scope tables, and lists are possible implementation choices, but the common keyed lookup structure asked for here is the hash table.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A stack manages nested scope order, while the keyed mapping within a scope commonly uses hashing.

evidence.quote: A symbol table maps names or symbol identities to attributes: type, scope, width, storage offset, parameter signature, constant information or linkage. A hash table gives expected O(1) insertion/lookup with suitable hashing; a stack of scope tables supports lexical nesting. Search the nearest scope first, insert declarations in the current scope, and remove visibility when leaving it.

Scanning may intern a spelling first; semantic analysis determines the declaration and type. Implementations differ, so first interaction is conventional rather than universal. Which of the following is an advantage of using an intermediate representation during the
compilation process?
questions.hint: Identify what the representation stores, what it omits and which later transformations it must support; separate a representation property from an algorithmic task.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 817

answer.explanation: COMP26 explains that IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. This supports retargeting and portability across platforms. Introducing IR does not inherently promise faster compilation, better error detection or lower memory use; it can add processing stages and data structures while improving architecture.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: An extra representation and processing stage do not inherently guarantee faster compilation.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Error detection depends on analyses and language rules; it is not the stated architectural advantage.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Separating source meaning from target lowering enables reuse across different platforms.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: IR introduces storage and does not guarantee reduced compiler memory consumption.

evidence.quote: IR separates source analysis from target implementation, allowing optimizers and backends to be reused. It should be easy to generate, analyze, transform and lower.

Ordinary TAC arithmetic has at most one operation, two sources and one destination: t1=c*d; t2=b+t1; a=t2. Quadruples store (op,arg1,arg2,result); triples omit an explicit result field and refer to instruction positions. Indirect triples reference a separate ordering list, easing rearrangement. Trees describe expressions; DAGs share common subexpressions, while quadruples/triples are instruction-record structures.

questions.stem: What is the shared compiler service that supports detecting, recovering from and reporting lexical, syntax and semantic errors?
questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 818

answer.explanation: Error handling and reporting is a shared service supporting multiple compilation phases. Scanning detects malformed tokens, parsing detects invalid token arrangements, and semantic analysis detects name, scope or type violations. These are contributors rather than one phase responsible for every error category. Naming the shared service makes D the appropriate complete answer without denying the diagnostic responsibilities of the other phases.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Lexical analysis handles lexical errors but is not the complete shared service.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Syntax analysis handles parsing errors but is not the complete shared service.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Semantic analysis handles semantic errors but is not the complete shared service.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Error handling names the shared support service.

evidence.quote: Panic-mode recovery skips input until a synchronizing token such as ; or } permits parsing to resume. Phrase-level recovery makes a local insertion/deletion. Report the location and cause while avoiding cascades of misleading diagnostics. Lexical, syntax and semantic phases each detect their own errors; error handling is a shared service.

Lex/flex generates scanners from patterns and actions. Yacc means Yet Another Compiler Compiler; Yacc/Bison generates parsers from grammar rules and semantic actions. Typical specification files have definitions, %% rules, and %% user code. Classic Yacc uses LALR; Bison supports additional LR and generalized modes. Scanner generation does not replace the CFG parser.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about syntax-directed translation?

options.label: A
options.text: It only involves the lexical analysis phase.

options.label: B
options.text: It involves the generation of intermediate code from the parse tree.

options.label: C
options.text: It is concerned with the optimization of the generated code.

options.label: D
options.text: It is performed during the code generation phase.

questions.hint: Track where each computed value comes from and when each production action runs. Distinguish the representation from its attached information.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 819

answer.text: It can generate intermediate code using parse-tree structure and semantic actions.
answer.explanation: COMP25 says syntax-directed actions may compute types, values, AST pointers or generated code. Generating IR from grammatical structure is therefore a supported use of syntax-directed translation. B describes that standard use without limiting it to lexical analysis or a single final phase. Optimization may use other analyses, and syntax-directed translation is not defined solely by optimization.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Syntax-directed translation is tied to grammatical productions and semantic actions, not solely tokenization.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Semantic actions associated with parsed structure can compute and emit an intermediate representation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Optimization is not the defining task; translation actions can construct many forms of semantic output.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: It is not restricted to final target-code generation; actions can run while parsing and constructing IR.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed translation scheme embeds executable actions in productions; the actions run while translating a source program, not while generating the compiler. Attributes may compute types, values, AST pointers or generated code. The scheme defines an input-to-output translation, not merely an input language.

Create an identifier leaf with mkleaf(id,entry), a number with mkleaf(num,value), and an operator node with mknode(op,left,right). For a−4+c, construct +(−(a,4),c). Postorder traversal prints postfix: a 4 − c +. A stack evaluator pushes operands and pops right then left operands for an operator. Infix-to-postfix is useful for stack machines but not mandatory for all compilers.

questions.stem: What is the general defining role of semantic rules attached to productions in a syntax-directed definition, rather than one possible specialized use?

options.label: A
options.text: To define the syntactic structure of the language.

options.label: B
options.text: To define computations of attributes such as types, values, environments and generated code.

options.label: C
options.text: To perform optimization techniques on the intermediate code.

options.label: D
options.text: To define the order of evaluation of expressions.

questions.hint: Track where each computed value comes from and when each production action runs. Distinguish the representation from its attached information.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 820

answer.text: To define computations of attributes such as types, values, environments and generated code.
answer.explanation: The grammar productions define syntactic structure, while semantic rules define computations of attributes associated with grammar symbols. Those attributes may represent types, values, environments or generated code. Assigning types and constraining evaluation dependencies are examples rather than exhaustive definitions. Optimization may occur in a particular translation, but is not the general defining role of all such rules.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Productions, rather than semantic rules, specify the grammatical structure.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Computing attributes is the general defining role.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Optimization is a possible specialized transformation, not the general definition.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Evaluation order is a specialized concern rather than the complete role.

evidence.quote: A syntax-directed definition is a CFG with attributes on grammar symbols and semantic rules on productions. An annotated parse tree displays computed attribute values; it is not itself an inherited or synthesized attribute. Synthesized attributes flow from children to a parent; inherited attributes carry context from parent or siblings.

For E→E1+T, E.val=E1.val+T.val synthesizes an expression value. A declaration’s type environment passed into its body is inherited. S-attributed definitions use only synthesized attributes and fit LR reduction-time evaluation naturally; suitable LL parsers can also compute them. L-attributed definitions restrict dependencies so a left-to-right traversal can evaluate inherited context. Attribute dependency cycles can prevent evaluation.

questions.stem: Which phase of the compiler is responsible for type checking?
questions.hint: Check operand compatibility and permitted conversions under the stated language rules; distinguish grammatical structure from semantic meaning.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 821

answer.explanation: PDF p6 explicitly names type checking as a major task of semantic analysis.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Lexical analysis recognizes tokens (p5).

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Syntax analysis checks grammatical hierarchy (p5).

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Type checking is explicitly assigned here (p6).

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Code generation converts IC to machine code (p7).

evidence.quote: A type checker verifies that operations are defined for their operands. In a simple strict language, integer mod requires two integers; array indexing requires an array and integer index; an if condition requires Boolean; assignment requires equal or convertible types. Function calls check parameter count and compatibility, and returns match result types.

Type inference derives types from constraints: if x is integer and + expects numeric operands, infer the expression type from numeric promotion rules. It is a static technique even without explicit annotations. Operator overloading supplies multiple operation meanings, not a substitute for type checking. int x="hello" is a type mismatch in ordinary C++/Java; division by zero and bounds violations are not automatically operand-type mismatches.

questions.stem: Which attribute is specifically recorded for each variable in a type-oriented symbol table and distinguishes its typing information from the name that identifies the entry?

options.label: A
options.text: To store the types of variables used in the program.

options.label: B
options.text: To store the names of variables used in the program.

options.label: C
options.text: To store the intermediate code generated during parsing.

options.label: D
options.text: To store the syntax rules of the programming language.

questions.hint: Ask whether the required information is a declaration’s identity and attributes, program structure or the ordered source tokens.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 824

answer.text: To store the types of variables used in the program.
answer.explanation: A symbol table associates a name or declaration identity with attributes. In a type-oriented table, the relevant attribute is the variable’s type, used to check whether operations and assignments are compatible. Names identify the records but do not themselves give typing information. Intermediate instructions and grammar rules belong to other representations and are not the per-variable typing attribute requested.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Variable types provide the requested typing attribute.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Names identify entries but are not their type attributes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: IR instructions are not the per-variable type attribute.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Syntax rules describe the language rather than variable types.

evidence.quote: A symbol table maps names or symbol identities to attributes: type, scope, width, storage offset, parameter signature, constant information or linkage. A hash table gives expected O(1) insertion/lookup with suitable hashing; a stack of scope tables supports lexical nesting. Search the nearest scope first, insert declarations in the current scope, and remove visibility when leaving it.

Scanning may intern a spelling first; semantic analysis determines the declaration and type. Implementations differ, so first interaction is conventional rather than universal. Not every punctuation token needs a symbol-table entry; literals may use a separate literal table. A hash table is an implementation, not the information’s semantic role.

questions.stem: Which advantage of static type checking specifically concerns detecting incompatible operations before the program executes?

options.label: C
options.text: Early detection of potential runtime errors.

questions.hint: Check operand compatibility and permitted conversions under the stated language rules; distinguish grammatical structure from semantic meaning.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 826

answer.text: Early detection of potential runtime errors.
answer.explanation: Static type checking can reject an incompatible operation during compilation, before that operation causes a run-time type error. This is the direct timing benefit asked for. Type information may also aid optimization, and diagnostics may make debugging easier, but those are additional consequences rather than the specific before-execution detection property. Type checking does not by itself guarantee faster code or eliminate all possible run-time errors.

choices.explanation: Optimization may use types but is a different benefit from the requested early rejection.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Compile-time rejection detects incompatible operations before execution.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Debugging may be easier, but that broad consequence does not specify the requested detection timing.

options.label: A
options.text: Assigning a floating-point value to an integer variable.

options.label: B
options.text: Assigning a value to an uninitialized variable.

options.label: C
options.text: Declaring a variable without specifying its type.

options.label: D
options.text: Using an undeclared variable in the program.

questions.hint: Check operand compatibility and permitted conversions under the stated language rules; distinguish grammatical structure from semantic meaning.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 828

answer.text: Converting a floating-point value when assigning to an integer variable, where the language permits it.
answer.explanation: COMP23 gives C++ int x=3.14 as an ordinary conversion yielding 3 when representable. That is the listed example of conversion, with the language caveat that Java needs a permitted cast and C++ brace initialization rejects narrowing. The remaining choices concern initialization, inference or undeclared names rather than converting one value type to another.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Floating-to-integer assignment performs conversion where permitted; exact legality and precision loss depend on the language.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: First assigning to a variable is initialization or assignment, not inherently a change of value type.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Omitting an explicit declaration type may invoke inference; it does not itself convert a value.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An undeclared name is a name-resolution problem rather than an example of value conversion.

evidence.quote: Coercion is an implicit conversion permitted by the language; a cast requests an explicit conversion. Widening often increases representable range, but can still lose precision: Java int→float is widening although large integers round. Java int→long is exact. Narrowing can lose range or fractional information.

In C++ ordinary int x=3.14 converts to 3 when representable; it is not inherently a type error. int x{3.14} is rejected as narrowing. C++ floating-to-integer conversion discards the fraction and has undefined behavior if the truncated value is unrepresentable. Java ordinary double→int assignment needs a permitted explicit cast. Mixing char and int is ordinarily valid after promotion in C++/Java; do not import a fictitious universal ban.

questions.stem: Which listed approaches are bottom-up and therefore are not top-down parsers? Select all that apply. Assume predictive recursive descent for A.
questions.hint: Use construction direction, lookahead and grammar restrictions. Distinguish algorithm families, implementations and coverage before comparing them.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 121

answer.explanation: Shift-reduce parsing starts from the input and reduces recognized handles toward the start symbol. LR is a bottom-up family using that strategy. Recursive descent and nonrecursive prediction instead expand productions top-down for suitable grammars. Therefore both B and D fail the top-down description. This directional distinction avoids an unsupported efficiency ranking between recursive and table-driven predictive implementations.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Predictive recursive descent is top-down.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Shift-reduce is bottom-up.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Nonrecursive prediction is top-down.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: LR is bottom-up.

evidence.quote: Top-down parsing starts with S and expands productions toward the input, usually constructing a leftmost derivation. Recursive descent typically has one procedure per nonterminal. A general recursive-descent implementation can backtrack; a predictive parser chooses a production using lookahead without backtracking. LL(1) scans Left to right, produces a Leftmost derivation and uses one lookahead token.
Bottom-up parsing starts from input and reduces toward S, constructing a rightmost derivation in reverse.

questions.stem:
Which one of the following is a type of compiler that compiles only the changed lines from
source code and updates the object code accordingly?
questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 267

answer.explanation: COMP02 defines incremental compilation as recompiling affected fragments or dependent units after edits. This is the compiler category intended by updating code after source changes. The question’s only changed lines wording is simplified: real dependency tracking can require recompiling more than literal edited lines. Retargeting and one-pass organization describe different properties.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Retargetable compilers support changing target descriptions rather than selecting edited source fragments.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: One pass counts traversals of the program, not whether edits trigger selective recompilation.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Incremental compilation updates affected fragments after edits, accounting for dependencies beyond literal changed lines.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Parallelizing compilation is not the category defined by selective recompilation after source changes.

evidence.quote: A preprocessor handles directives such as file inclusion and macros. An assembler translates assembly to object code. A linker combines object files and libraries, resolves external symbols and performs relocation. A loader maps an executable into memory and starts it. Compilation alone does not necessarily produce a ready executable.

A cross-compiler runs on a host platform and generates code for a different target. Multiple targets require appropriate backends, not a special definition of cross-compilation. A retargetable compiler supports changing target descriptions. Incremental compilation recompiles affected fragments or dependent units after edits; it is more than literally replacing changed lines. One-pass versus multipass counts traversals, not supported targets.

questions.stem:
Which technique of code optimization shifts computations from run time to compile time by
evaluating constant expressions at compile time and replacing them with their values?
questions.hint: Trace whether computation is evaluated, moved, shared or removed. Preserve observable effects and use the stated arithmetic and target assumptions.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 268

answer.explanation: PDF p18 lists constant folding and illustrates R2 = 3 * 2. Evaluating this constant expression early gives 6, eliminating that runtime computation. B describes this operation as compile time evaluation, although constant folding would be the module’s exact name.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: P18 copy propagation example copies r1 into r2, not evaluates a constant arithmetic expression.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Evaluating 3 * 2 to 6 is the constant-folding example on p18, matching the stem.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: P18 code movement relocates a block outside a loop, not necessarily evaluating it at compilation.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: P18 dead-code elimination removes unreachable statements, rather than computing constant values.

evidence.quote: Constant folding evaluates constant expressions during compilation: 3*4→12. Constant propagation substitutes known values: x=3; y=x+2 becomes y=3+2 before folding. Copy propagation substitutes a copied name while its source remains unchanged. Dead-code elimination removes unreachable code or computations whose values are unused and whose evaluation has no necessary side effects.

questions.stem: For const int x=8; const int y=16; if(x>y){int z=x+y;}, which techniques directly evaluate the known condition and remove its unreachable body? Select all that apply. Arithmetic simplification means algebraic identity rewriting here.
questions.hint: Trace whether computation is evaluated, moved, shared or removed. Preserve observable effects and use the stated arithmetic and target assumptions.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 263

answer.text: Dead code elimination; Compile time evaluation
answer.explanation: Both x and y are known constants, so evaluating 8>16 at compile time yields false. The body can never execute and dead-code elimination can remove it. These are distinct but compatible transformations, corresponding to B and C in this option order. Code motion relocates computations, while algebraic identity simplification is not the decisive operation on this constant-false condition.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: No relocation is needed to evaluate or delete the branch.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The unreachable branch body can be removed.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The condition is evaluated from known constants at compile time.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: No algebraic identity rewrite is the decisive step.

evidence.quote: For const int x=8,y=16; if(x>y){int z=x+y;}, propagate the constants, fold 8>16 to false, then remove the unreachable branch. Both compile-time evaluation and dead-code elimination apply.
Algebraic simplification removes identities when valid: integer x+0→x.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
questions.hint: Identify each activity’s input and output. Distinguish character recognition, grammatical structure, semantic checks and target implementation.

answer.text: A compiler translates; an interpreter executes a representation.
answer.explanation: COMP01 distinguishes translating source into an equivalent target from executing a program representation. Bytecode systems may combine compilation, interpretation and JIT, so the distinction is not simply all-at-once versus line-by-line execution.
